## 📋 How to Report Memory Issues in Zen

To help us investigate memory-related issues effectively, please follow these steps carefully:

### 1. Gather Troubleshooting Information

1. Open Zen and go to: [`about:support`](https://support.mozilla.org/kb/use-troubleshooting-information-page-fix-firefox)  
2. Click **"Copy text to clipboard"**  
3. Paste the copied text into the template

### 2. Capture Memory Report

1. Open a new tab and go to: `about:memory`  
2. Click the **"Measure and save…"** button  
3. With the downloaded file, drag and drop it into the template

### 3. Submit Your Report

In your comment under this issue, include both reports using the template below:


````
<Describe a bit your situation and whats wrong. Maybe also include a https://profiler.firefox.com/ if necessary>

<details>
<summary>About Support</summary>

```
REPLACE WITH ABOUT:SUPPORT CONTENTS
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>About memory</summary>

REPLACE WITH ABOUT:MEMORY FILE UPLOAD
</details>
````

## Before You Submit

- **Stay on topic.** Please keep this thread focused on memory issue reports only.
- **Use a clean testing environment.** Disable all **addons, custom themes, and mods** (`about:addons`) — these are known to affect performance.

## Optional: Test on the Latest Twilight Build

To help determine if your memory issue has already been addressed in recent changes, please try reproducing the problem using the **latest Twilight build**:

🔗 [Download Twilight build](https://zen-browser.app/download/?twilight)

<details>
<summary>About Support</summary>

*I summed the processes 'resident-unique' values. In Windows this is called the active private working set: the amount of physical memory in use by the process that can't be used by other processes. This is also the value shown in task manager. 
This value is also know as the Unique Set Size (USS).
†These can include pinned/essential tabs that are not loaded after startup, but their tab objects exist and are prepared to be loaded. These not-yet-loaded pins consume ~10MB a piece. Explicitly unloaded tabs are completely 'destroyed' and consume ~0MB.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ff98c5a-d9f1-428e-b7c8-86da3d5127ea)

I did not make totals of measures like 'resident-phys-footprint' (Mac's default memory shown per process) or 'resident' (resident set size (RSS) / working set: the amount of physical memory currently mapped by a process), because adding these values up would double-count shared memory. 
You can see remarks about this in Mozilla's own [memory telemetry code](https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/integration/autoland/file/tip/xpcom/base/MemoryTelemetry.cpp#l496) and a [detailed explanation](https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-platform/c/WGNOtjHdsdA) in a post on choices made in MacOS memory usage telemetry.

All in all I do not find these reports show unreasonable high memory usage. 

Notes:
1. @Illustar0 's figure looks high to me. According to the report most of it was caused by 4 GitHub pages (2 Copilot) using 3.8GB in total. 
2. 3.7GB of the memory use belonged to the GPU process. From the support info it shows the UHD integrated (CPU) graphics are active and not the dedicated nvidia RTX 3050 GPU, which explains why quite some shared system RAM is used as GPU memory.  
3. A relatively large portion of the main process's memory usage (and events) can be attributed to the DevTools.  Its orphan DOM nodes and JavaScript running in it; 500MB.

@Beeditor04  On startup pins/essentials show in `about:processes` even while not opened. They already get created empty but ready to go. In the process manager you see they're assigned some 34MB. This is mostly unmapped memory though. Actually active memory (resident unique) is around 10MB. Once they actually load this'll typically increase to 150MB or more.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f524ad67-a797-4458-98b4-602e3a50d66a)

In Firefox all pinned tabs get loaded by default instead of on demand, but if you change that preference flag to true (`browser.sessionstore.restore_pinned_tabs_on_demand`, defaults false in FF , true in Zen) you see the same behaviour. I guess creating the tab/window up front in an empty state is done for speed. 

3.7GB of your Zen's memory usage came from the GPU process. The support info shows your iGPU (UHD graphics) on the CPU was active and not your dGPU RTX 3050. This explains why quite some system RAM was used as Shared GPU memory.

Evn on idle with no tabs, and 6 extensions memory usage is around 4.1GB

About memory [20250904 1414 memory-report.json.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22146902/20250904.1414.memory-report.json.gz)

> Has the dev team looked into the fact that this might be an upstream issue? I am having the same issues with [LibreWolf](https://librewolf.net/), a firefox derivative.

> This usually happens when I let the browser open for long periods of time, even when not using. (I never turn off the computer)
> So it starts adding up RAM usage

Before switching to Zen, I used “stock” Firefox and had similar issues back then. When Firefox was open for a long period of time (several weeks/months) without restarting (which I don't think is unusual on a MacBook), it started to consume enormous amounts of RAM (10+ out of 16 GB on my system) and became slow and almost froze. So maybe part of the problem actually has to do with upstream Firefox?

When I switched to Zen, I was concerned that I would also have these memory and performance issues due to the Firefox base. And here we are. But surprisingly, I feel that the memory situation is better in Zen, but after a while, it also becomes slower and sluggish.

I will definitely keep an eye on it.

* why resident unique and not physical footprint I summed the processes 'resident-unique' values. In Windows this is called the active private working set: the amount of physical memory in use by the process that can't be used by other processes. This is also the value shown in task manager. This value is also know as the Unique Set Size (USS). ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ff98c5a-d9f1-428e-b7c8-86da3d5127ea) I did not make totals of measures like 'resident-phys-footprint' (Mac's default memory shown per process) or 'resident' (resident set size (RSS) / working set: the amount of physical memory currently mapped by a process), because adding these values up would double-count shared memory. You can see remarks about this in Mozilla's own [memory telemetry code](https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/integration/autoland/file/tip/xpcom/base/MemoryTelemetry.cpp#l496) and a [detailed explanation](https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-platform/c/WGNOtjHdsdA) in a post on choices made in MacOS memory usage telemetry.
† about pinned tabs These can include pinned/essential tabs that are not loaded after startup, but their tab objects exist and are prepared to be loaded. These not-yet-loaded pins consume ~10MB a piece. Explicitly unloaded tabs are completely 'destroyed' and consume ~0MB.

About memory [memory-report.json.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22387140/memory-report.json.gz)

> Before switching to Zen, I used “stock” Firefox and had similar issues back then. When Firefox was open for a long period of time (several weeks/months) without restarting (which I don't think is unusual on a MacBook), it started to consume enormous amounts of RAM (10+ out of 16 GB on my system) and became slow and almost froze. So maybe part of the problem actually has to do with upstream Firefox?
> 
> I will definitely keep an eye on it.

For testing, I had two tabs open: GitHub and a SPA I'm currently working on, which reloads on every code change and has DevTools running alongside it. I've been leaving Zen minimised in the background over the last few days. The Activity Monitor now shows that almost 6 GB of memory are used by Zen. The memory report shows over 3 GB of total resident memory. However, I've noticed that it fluctuates a lot when I do multiple measurements (ranging from 2 to 4 GB). I'm not sure if this is intentional. To me, the report looks like a memleak in DevTools, as it consumes over 2 GB and is trending upwards. _(Once, it even consumed about 5 GB, but unfortunately I didn't save the report.)_

It seems that there is also an upstream bug report for this, but it has not been fixed since 6 years (!): https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1595797

Looks like there are several different memory leaks? A quick search on Bugzilla for memory leaks lists about 200 unresolved reported defects, which I think underlines this unfortunately.

Last version fixed a memory leak related to folder icons where the refresh tick would be called on ever frame. Would be nice if y'all could start sending profiler reports as well:

https://profiler.firefox.com/

I'll repeat what I said in my separate issue here so it's in one place: Zen seems to leave thousands (I've counted 1499 zen.exe instances running at one point using RAMMap) of processes with remaining kernel memory allocation, and presumably also some corresponding services. Using a large amount of memory and slowing down my system. These processes don't show up in Task Manager, only when using RAMMap. Turning off extensions doesn't seem to affect the behaviour. I am unsure what all of the exact actions that cause more processes to spawn are, but from testing I've concluded that: opening new tabs (or clicking on unloaded tabs) adds multiple processes to the list, following links in the same tab doesn't seem to create new processes, sometimes a new process appears when doing either nothing or actions that previously didn't spawn a new process, unsure why that is. It also seems that the process count increases over time, but I'm not 100% sure, I'm guessing these processes are all just regular stuff for a browser, just that they aren't getting cleaned up propperly. Notably I have to highlight that the number of processes I can see in RAMMap never decreases, not even when closing Zen, the number keeps increasing untill a full system restart, meaning that when I'm using my PC over the day, if I try to game at the end of the day it becomes unplayable because I have no RAM left. Here are the numbers I got from some testing: win startup -> 0 zen.exe instances found in RAMMap output zen launched -> 15 3 tabs opened -> 22 zen closed -> 22 reopened -> 34 another tab opened -> 42 closed zen after waiting some time -> 42 reopened and played a video -> 66 test 2: open -> 16 reopen -> 24 time passed -> 24 open yt -> 28 watch for 2 mins -> 28 jump around links within youtube -> 28 close zen -> 28 clicked some unloaded tabs, opened new ones -> 85 open Wikipedia -> 90 following links within wikipedia -> 90 opening new website by following link on wikipedia (same tab) -> 91 going back 10 times -> 91 In testing I wasn't able to easily get to a thousand processes, I'm not sure if something special happened the times I got to that high a number or whether I was just using my browser a lot, but I've experienced severe memory usage problems multiple times over the past month, causing frame drops in games from lack of available RAM. Since I had originally posted the issue, I have once again had it jump up to 544 processes in RAMMap just by regular everyday use. This session is the one I've provided the troubleshooting and memory information for, but from a quick glance at it, I don't think it's visible in the memory report, as I don't think it's something Zen/Firefox is able to track. @Redex68 Looks like you discovered a case of zombie processes; Processes where all threads are closed, but the process itself is not. The mem usage is in "Standby" which is like a cache where previous items are not thrown out of memory yet for faster performance if needed again. This is low priority and gets evicted easily when another process really needs the space. It's therefore also not counted towards memory usage when looking at tools like task manager. (it's called "cached" in the performance > memory tab) I can recreate this, but not in the thousands. As a result also not with such a large page table size. When closing Zen I regularly get 1 or 2 new zombies from the main and GPU processes. Have you been able to correlate the process IDs with the process description in Zen's process manager? p.s. I also see the same happening when testing in Firefox, but to a lesser degree.
@Propheticus would be worth to report this to firefox

> This is low priority and gets evicted easily when another process really needs the space.
It's therefore also not counted towards memory usage when looking at tools like task manager.

> Doubt it makes a difference since this thread is from Jun 8 and this is still a problem, either that or other legitimate issues are just being rolled into here instead of being researched.

@Rydsmith There isn't a single root cause here. People are reporting a variety of symptoms, and they're all getting grouped together. Some cases are real memory leaks, others are just normal spikes caused by heavy workloads, and some are probably unrelated bugs that only appear similar on the surface. The point is: there's no universal "Zen is slow" or "Zen uses too much RAM" problem. There are many environmental factors and user mistakes involved, and it's not as simple as "just fix it".

This is a `[meta]` issue, as the title indicates. It's a place where reports can be collected, and when we have time, we look through them for actual anomalies. Most of them boil down to users installing lots of mods, add-ons, themes, and so on, without realizing the performance impact these can have on the browser. That's not necessarily a Zen issue; in general, the more you install, the slower things get.

This issue likely won't ever be closed or resolved, because it isn't meant to address one specific bug. If a genuine, reproducible issue is found, a separate report will be created for proper investigation and fixing.

That said, giving a bit more of background, explanations, about:processes, etc when commenting or even posting a profiler report (https://profiler.firefox.com/) would help even more as just giving out an about:memory is as useful as just showing a screenshot of the task manager (not very useful).

I have been sort of plagued by a memory leak (I think?) as well. However reproducing it is really difficult, because it happens only sometimes and additionally only after having Zen open for a really long time, like +5hrs (with usually my device going to sleep in between). When it happens I can see Zen using 20GB minimum, which is quite alot but I guess that's because I have many tabs open at the same time. But then, to make matters worse, when I close Zen to free the memory _sometimes_ it would stay open in background and just start eating memory, like it gains memory each few seconds one more GB and I have to kill it via command. I do wonder though if this could be caused by my extensions, however I did not have these problems with the same extensions in Floorp (which in general I feel like used less memory, I could be wrong though). Hi, I've been using Zen Browser for a while now, and its been the best browser that I have used so far. In the past I've experienced high RAM usage with zen on my Mac, causing system alerts about memory overload occasionally, but I was told that its a common issue so I didn't really bother much as I only needed to restart the browser. However, ever since v1.18.2b which I updated just an hour ago, I have had to quit and reopen zen more than half a dozen times due to excessive RAM usage slowing down my computer. Really appreciate what you guys are doing, and hope that there is a fix to this soon. Thanks!

Hi, I've been using Zen for maybe half a year now and it's never been worse on mac in terms of energy. Having a few tabs open consumes more energy than my heavy docker containers. Here's some data, if it helps:

I use FF, Opera, Vivaldi, Brave continuously and simultaneously with lots of tabs open in each. For a new context, I need a fresh browser, so after hunting around chanced upon Zen.

Fresh Zen installation (Win 11, 32GB memory, Intel Ultra 5) with no extensions - 4 tabs open and it hit 3.7GB which seemed excessive, so I started hunting around and found this issue. 

However, subsequently it has reduced to 2.3GB. To cross check I opened the same in Brave (which already has many tabs open). Here's a tab by tab snapshot comparison:

| Tab                    | Brave | Zen  |
| ----------------------- | ----- | ---- |
| Stripe                  | 631   | 703  |
| 2 google workspace tabs | 870   | 950  |
| Zoho desk               | 218   | 230  |
|                         | 1719  | 1883 |

Seems to be by and large the same.

As a separate datapoint, Windows reports 2.3GB for Zen, and 1.9GB for Brave (with these 4 tabs + a dozen more)

My system is Pop!_OS 24.04 with the COSMIC desktop environment, and the Linux kernel is 6.18.7. Today I newly installed and started using the Zen browser, and I noticed that the memory usage is astonishing. I only have four tabs open and seven extensions installed, yet the memory usage is around 5 GB, and it gradually increases over time. Previously, I was using Firefox with the same extensions and a similar number of pages, and the memory usage was about 2 GB.

@zero-hugo please follow what is said in the opening post of this issue. 
We can't help based on these screenshots.

The memory leak issue is really annoying. It's fine for a day or two, or three, but at some point it just baloons until there is no free RAM left. I had to restart the PC a few times because zen hogged it all, OOMKiller didn't do anything about it (that may be a skill issue on my part), and I failed to kill zen in time before the computer stopped responding completely. 

I spent some time in troubleshoot mode, didn't touch any settings, and memory leak still seems to be present.
 
I started at about 4 gb and after 1.5 days RAM usage increased to 9gb, at which point i stopped the experiment. During that time I mostly just watched YT and did a few searches.

_Interesting observation:_ RAM usage didn't grow linearly. For a day it was staying at stable 5-6gb, next day it was the same for hours. And then I open 4 tabs and usage rises to 9gb. After restarting and reopening the same tabs, ram didn't grow to the same 9gb and stayed at about 5-7gb.

The tab count was about 30ish, of them about 8-15 were active, depending on my YT queue and active searches.

I didn't test zen to complete failure, until it hogs all the free RAM I have, because it was too painful to use without an adblocker and on default settings(disabled hw acceleration), especially for a few days, but I still don't think this is normal for a browser to use 9gb of RAM for that much tabs. I was using firefox with the same set of extensions until approximately a year ago and it didn't do that.

Another interesting observation: when I was saving a memory report, i saw 9gb used by zen in Resources app. about:memory, however, reported only about 4.3gb of total resident memory. 
Not sure, how Resources counts application (not process) memory, but it seems legit to me, because when it reported zen using 12+gb of RAM and close to 100% overall memory (I have 16gb), it strongly correlated to my computer hanging entirely.

@michaelhazan  In your  case it looks like a Github actions tab has 5 'ghost' pages and is holding on to a lot of orphan (JS) objects that are not cleared from memory. Could the Refined Github extension be playing a role here?

@rexendevar There's some mentions of (webrender) features being on a blocklist for your iGPU / driver.  eg for reason "FEATURE_FAILURE_BROKEN_DRIVER". 
These blocklists exist to disable features that have known issues (like crashes, mem leaks, instability) on certain hardware/drivers/os or combinations of those. 
I see you ignored those by altering these preferences: 

```
gfx.webgpu.ignore-blocklist: true
gfx.webrender.all: true
```
And set all webrender features on forcefully.  
Advise: revert these 2 settings to their default.

also delete these entries so they can be re-evaluated:
```
gfx.blacklist.accelerated-canvas2d.failureid: FEATURE_FAILURE_DL_BLOCKLIST_NO_ID
gfx.blacklist.dmabuf.failureid: FEATURE_FAILURE_DL_BLOCKLIST_NO_ID
gfx.blacklist.gl.threadsafe.failureid: FEATURE_FAILURE_DL_BLOCKLIST_NO_ID
```
